title: Write a Multi-Container Pod with an Init Container
intro: Init containers are a common trip-up when hand-writing YAML — they live in their own top-level list, not nested inside the main containers list.

steps.prompt: Create a Pod named 'app' with an init container named 'wait-for-db' (image busybox) that runs before the main container, and a main container named 'server' (image myapp:1.0) exposing container port 8080.
steps.hint: spec.initContainers is a separate top-level list under spec, a sibling of spec.containers — not nested inside it and not the same list.
steps.solution:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: app
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: wait-for-db
    image: busybox
    command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 2"]
  containers:
  - name: server
    image: myapp:1.0
    ports:
    - containerPort: 8080
steps.explanation: initContainers run one at a time, in order, and all must exit successfully before any container in spec.containers starts — that's the entire mechanism from tutorial-022, expressed as YAML instead of just observed via describe.
steps.why: This is the field beginners most often nest incorrectly by hand — putting an init container inside spec.containers with some extra flag, rather than in its own spec.initContainers list, is a very common hand-editing mistake under time pressure.
